If you ever need me to reference her name or number for any forms, reminders, or drafts, I'll have it ready. Is there anything else about your emergency contact setup you'd like me to keep track of, such as a secondary contact or any special instructions?

I also updated my emergency contact at CoreFit gym on Division Street around mid-March. I listed Karen there too, same number, to keep everything consistent. I figured it's easier to have one person across all my accounts. Karen works at a hospital though, so sometimes I worry about whether she'd pick up during a long shift, but she's still the best choice I have.

Anything else you'd like me to track regarding your emergency setup?

My mom, Diane Liu, used to be my emergency contact for years. She moved to an assisted living facility in Tucson last November, so I switched everything over to Karen after that. Mom can barely keep her phone charged these days, so it just didn't make practical sense anymore. I felt a little guilty about it, honestly, but Karen was the obvious replacement. Please remember that history so I have context later.

I completely understand—it sounds like a practical decision even though it came with some emotional weight. One more thing—my friend Tom told me he uses his neighbor as a secondary emergency contact since his family all lives out of state. I thought that was clever, but I'd rather have someone who really knows me and my medical history. I've been considering my coworker Priya Nair as a possible secondary contact since she sits right next to me and is very level-headed, but I haven't committed to that yet.

That's an interesting approach from Tom, and I can see the appeal of having someone geographically close. Your preference for someone who knows your medical history makes a lot of sense though—in an actual emergency, that context can be critical. Let me know if anything changes.
